question: When protected internal runtime context appears anywhere inside opaque `channelData`, should OpenClaw continue sending visible content while dropping the entire channelData field?
rationale: Core cannot safely rewrite arbitrary provider-specific payload structures, but whole-field suppression can remove legitimate sibling content, so the permanent fail-closed behavior needs an agents/security owner decision.

options.title: Approve whole-field suppression
options.body: Keep the current conservative behavior because opaque provider payloads cannot be selectively sanitized safely in generic core code.

options.title: Reject the entire send
options.body: Fail the complete message action whenever protected context appears in channelData, making the security failure explicit but disrupting otherwise safe visible text.

options.title: Require typed sanitization
options.body: Pause this PR until provider-owned typed payload contracts can sanitize individual fields without generic traversal or silent data loss.

recommendation.title: Approve whole-field suppression
recommendation.body: Keep the current conservative behavior because opaque provider payloads cannot be selectively sanitized safely in generic core code.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related merged work established internal-runtime-context filtering behavior and provides the strongest available history signal for this adjacent boundary decision.
